children: Canada-based convenience store giant Alimentation Couche-Tard has offered $7.5 billion to $8 billion to acquire Cumberland Farms, The Times reported Saturday.
Headquartered in Charlotte, N.C., Cumberland Farms is the former EG Group, a global convenience-store chain previously based in the UK.
Neither company responded to an inquiry about the proposal by publication time.
Cumberland Farms had filed for an initial public offering with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in July for a listing on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol "CMBY."

Couche-Tard has been among the most active players in downstream energy and convenience retail acquisitions. It launched a voluntary tender offer in July to acquire a controlling interest in Poland's Zabka Group for about US$8.7 billion.

In early October, it agreed to acquire 52 retail sites, 16 cardlock sites and 71 fuel supply contracts from Irving Oil. And in 2025, the company completed its $1.57 billion purchase of GetGo from Giant Eagle.
Couche-Tard withdrew its more than $40 billion takeover offer for Seven & i Holdings, the parent company of 7-Eleven, in July last year.
The global retailer also attempted to acquire EG Group in 2022 for about twice the recent $8 billion offer, The Times noted.
